_comment: Static audio build manifest (DOJP-35). One entry per deliverable. Timeline steps: {sfx} | {tts} | {robot_tts} | {silence_ms}, each with optional gain_db / fade_out_ms. Optional bed: an SFX looped under the whole timeline. {tts} renders in the entry's narrator voice (per voice folder); {robot_tts} always renders in the scanner-robot ElevenLabs voice (robot_voice_id below) regardless of narrator. Mastered to the app's TARGET_DBFS; exported stereo via free_pool.export_audio_segment (DOJP-56). Robot lines spell the brand 'Yo-toe' (phonetic respelling so ElevenLabs says Yoh-Toe; Callum picked it by ear 2026-10-08) - Hugo's tts lines keep 'Yoto'.

scanning.description: The /scanning warm-up clip. Airport call under Hugo's deputy/new-sky monologue, robot activation + deep-scan, robot scan line, radio static with five deep-scans. Script rewritten 2026-10-02 (Hamish reference removed - evergreen).

timeline.tts: Air Traffic Controller {narrator} here, and how splendid - [chuckle] my trusty co-pilot has reported for duty! Here's the wonderful thing about the sky, old chum: it's never, ever quite the same. Every scan finds new jet planes, dashing off to new corners of the world on adventures all of their own. Shall we see who's soaring overhead today?
timeline.prompt: [speak as a jolly, eccentric elderly British gentleman with a posh RP accent - a retired pilot, warm and theatrical, brimming with delight, crisp consonants]

timeline.robot_tts: Scanning the skies for jet planes

scanning-again.description: Interstitial for a rescan: robot line (note: 'more'), then three contiguous deep-scan pulses. Matches the production file's transcript + envelope.

timeline.robot_tts: Scanning the skies for more jet planes

overandout.description: Session sign-off: Hugo's farewell (rewritten 2026-10-02, 'over and out' close), one deep-scan sting.

timeline.tts: My word, that was a fantastic session of jet plane spotting! [laugh] We found some magnificent flying machines up there. Start up your Yoto jet plane scanner again soon, because one never knows what celestial surprises await. {narrator}... over and out.
timeline.prompt: [speak as an eccentric elderly British gentleman with a posh RP accent - a retired pilot signing off, warm and satisfied, gently theatrical, fond and unhurried]

free-scanning.description: Free-tier scan intro: Hugo, then dial-tuning static. Free tier is tuning in, not scanning - no deep-scans (Callum 2026-10-03).

timeline.tts: Roger, roger. Air Traffic Controller {narrator} here. [chuckle] We've got some top secret flight paths cleared for us today. I've locked onto a few recently spotted jet planes from across the globe just for you. Hold steady while I tune these dials and bring them onto your Yoto, okay?
timeline.prompt: [speak as a jolly, eccentric elderly British gentleman with a posh RP accent - a retired pilot, warm and theatrical, brimming with delight, crisp consonants]

timeline.tts: Let's tune into another one, shall we?

free-overandout.description: Free-tier sign-off: Club pitch, over-and-out close, jazz bed, no sting (Callum 2026-10-03).

timeline.tts: Splendidly done, old sport. [laugh] Those were some delightful jet planes from across the globe we tuned into. And remember, if you are a Yoto Club member, head to the Club Collection area in the Yoto app to find your own personal jet plane scanner that spots planes in the skies above your Yoto. Or listen in again with me soon to tune in to some other planes. {narrator}, over and out.

timeline.tts: [clear throat] Good morning, good morning! Air Traffic Controller {narrator} here, and what a fine time for you to be at the controls with me, old chum. The skies are waking up: the very first jet planes of the day are stretching their wings, warming up their engines, and lifting off runways all over the world. Shall we see who's up bright and early today?

timeline.tts: Good evening, old chum. Air Traffic Controller {narrator} here, and you're on the night watch with me tonight, co-pilot, how splendid! [sigh] Here's a secret about the evening sky: it never goes to bed. Right now there are jet planes full of sleepy passengers, and great big cargo planes stuffed with parcels, humming along into the night. Shall we see who's flying as the day winds down?
